formula: Chances are that + subject + verb + other information

rules.zh: 核心表達是：【Chances are that + complete clause】 詞語【Chances】通常使用複數，而動詞使用 are。火車很可能會誤點。
rules.en: The fixed expression is “Chances are that” Chances are that + complete clause Chances are that the train will be late. Chance is that the train will be late.

rules.zh: 在【that】後面必須有完整的主語和動詞。商店很可能已經關門。
rules.en: “That” must be followed by a complete clause Chances are that the shop is closed. Chances are that the closed shop.

rules.zh: 目標表達【Chances are that】表示「很可能」，並不表示百分之百肯定。奧莉花很可能會加入我們。 這句表示說話者認為她加入的可能性頗高，但仍然有可能不加入。不要把表示完全確定的來源句改成 Chances are that。奧莉花一定會加入我們。 以【definitely】為例：比 chances are that 更肯定，兩者意思並不完全相同。
rules.en: The expression shows likelihood, not certainty Chances are that Chances are that Olivia will join us. Too strong: Olivia will definitely join us.

rules.zh: 現在式：他很可能在家。將來式：價格很可能會上升。過去式：他們很可能錯過了巴士。現在完成式：包裹很可能已經送到。情態動詞：這部機器很可能可以修理。
rules.en: The clause may describe the present, past or future Chances are that he is at home. Chances are that the price will rise. Chances are that they missed the bus. Present perfect Chances are that the parcel has already arrived. Modal verb Chances are that the machine can be repaired.

rules.zh: 這部舊電腦很可能不支援該程式。 不要把 not 放在 Chances are 中間。
rules.en: Negative meaning belongs inside the that-clause Chances are that + subject + will not / is not / did not... Chances are that the old computer will not support the program. Chances are not that the computer will support it.

rules.zh: 以下部分只是在核心句型前提供條件、證據、背景或對比，並不是固定表達的一部分。根據最新數據，銷售額很可能會上升。 銷售額很可能會上升。巴士很可能很快便會到達。 如果你現在離開，便很可能趕上較早的火車。
rules.en: Introductory phrases are optional extensions The following parts are not included in the fixed expression: If the weather remains dry, Based on the latest figures, With several people absent, Although the result is not final, Since the lights are still on, They simply provide the condition, evidence, background or contrast. Based on the latest figures, chances are that sales will increase. The sentence is also complete without the introductory phrase: Chances are that sales will increase. 1. Direct prediction Chances are that + clause. Chances are that the bus will arrive soon. 2. After a condition or time clause If / When / Once + clause, chances are that + clause. If you leave now, chances are that you will catch the earlier train.

rules.zh: 考慮到票價低廉，門票很可能會很快售罄。 雖然結果尚未確定，但這項建議很可能已獲得足夠支持。 天空愈來愈陰暗，所以很可能很快便會下雨。 這段旅程很可能不會需時太久。
rules.en: After an evidence or background phrase Based on / Given / With / Judging from + information, chances are that + clause. Given the low price, chances are that the tickets will sell quickly. 4. After a contrast or reason clause Although / Even though / Since / Because + clause, chances are that + clause. Although the results are not final, chances are that the proposal has enough support. 5. After another main clause Complete clause, so chances are that + clause. The sky is getting darker, so chances are that it will rain soon. 6. With negative meaning Chances are that + subject + negative verb. Chances are that the journey will not take long.

rules.zh: 在預測事情時，Chances are that 可配合過去式或現在完成式，表示某事很可能已發生。它與 probably意思相近，但 probably 是放在子句內的副詞，而 Chances are that 引出完整預測。It is likely that 較中性正式；There is a chance that 只表示有可能，語氣通常較弱。選用哪個結構時，要同時考慮文法位置、正式程度和可能性的強弱。
rules.en: With past or completed events Chances are that + subject + past verb / has or have + past participle. Chances are that the meeting has already ended. Related Structures 1. Chances are that vs probably Probably is an adverb placed inside a clause. The train will probably be late. Chances are that introduces a complete prediction. Chances are that the train will be late. The meanings are similar, but the grammar is different. 2. Chances are that vs It is likely that It is likely that is neutral and is often suitable for formal writing. It is likely that prices will rise. Chances are that is especially common in natural conversation and less formal writing. Chances are that prices will rise. 3. Chances are that vs There is a chance that There is a chance that may simply mean that something is possible. There is a chance that it will rain. Chances are that normally suggests a stronger likelihood. Chances are that it will rain.

rules.zh: 在其他變體中，The chances are that 是可以使用的較完整形式，但本練習採用較短的 Chances are that。口語中可省略 that 寫成 Chances are, ...，不過不列作本課答案。What are the chances that...? 是詢問機率的問句，與作出很可能會發生某事的陳述句Chances are that... 功能不同。
rules.en: “The chances are that” is also possible The fuller form is: The chances are that + clause The chances are that the plan will succeed. This exercise uses the shorter target: Chances are that + clause 5. “Chances are,...” is an informal variant In conversation, speakers sometimes omit that: Chances are, he has already left. This form is grammatical, but it is excluded from the answers in this exercise. Students must practise the complete target: Chances are that he has already left. 6. “What are the chances that...?” is a different structure What are the chances that the event will be cancelled? This is a question asking about probability. It is not the same as the statement: Chances are that the event will be cancelled.

benefits.zh: 讓你作出較審慎的預測這個句型讓你表達某件事很可能發生，同時避免令人誤以為你百分之百肯定。
benefits.en: It lets you make a careful prediction This structure allows you to say that something is likely without pretending that you are completely certain.

benefits.zh: 幫助你控制說法的肯定程度這項計劃會成功。 這項計劃很可能會成功。 第二句保留了一定程度的不確定性，因此說法較審慎和合理。
benefits.en: It helps control the strength of your claim Compare: The plan will succeed. Chances are that the plan will succeed. The second sentence leaves room for uncertainty and may therefore sound more careful and reasonable.

benefits.zh: 避免反覆使用 probably 你不需要在每個預測句中反覆使用 probably，可以運用 Chances are that 增加句式變化。
benefits.en: It gives you an alternative to repeatedly using “probably” Instead of placing probably in every prediction, you can use Chances are that to vary your sentence structure.

benefits.zh: 把證據和可能出現的結果連接起來你可以先提出證據，再說明最可能出現的結果。考慮到天空滿佈烏雲，很可能很快便會下雨。
benefits.en: It connects evidence with a likely result You can first mention the evidence and then state the likely conclusion. Given the dark clouds, chances are that it will rain soon.

benefits.zh: 適合日常對話和討論這個句型適合用來討論計劃、行為、天氣、工作、行程和可能出現的結果。
benefits.en: It is useful in everyday speaking and discussion The structure is useful when discussing plans, behaviour, weather, work, travel and possible results.

benefits.zh: 增加句子開首的變化這個表達不一定要放在整句最前面。你可以先提出條件、原因、對比或證據，再使用核心句型。
benefits.en: It allows different sentence openings The expression does not always have to appear at the beginning. You can place a condition, reason, contrast or piece of evidence before it.
